title: LAMP Protocol for Entomopathogenic Serratia
author: Nicholas P Doidge
materials: Make up stock solutions of the LAMP primers using MG H20. Add the same amount of MG H20 to the dried primers as the primer amount in moles to make 1000 µM stock solutions. Dilute the F3, B3, LF and LB primers 1:10 to make 100 µM working stocks.

Equipment Required: -Pipettors and pipette tips in a range of sizes (1000 µL, 100 µL, 10 µL) -Tissue homogenizer (Pacific Laboratory Products PLP-SWE-G6 Homogenizer, alternatively Qiagen Tissue Lyser II or a high-speed horizontal vortex if not using tissue homogeniser) -Low speed swing bucket centrifuge (500 x g) (ideally but can be done without) -High speed microcentrifuge (16000 x g) -Equipment for measuring DNA concentration and quality (e.g. Thermo Fisher Nanodrop or Implen Nanophotometer) -Heating element fitted to the tube size used for LAMP (PCR block, heating block, hot water bath) -Access to a fridge (4°C) and freezer (-20ºC) or ice to achieve these temperatures

Materials Required (per extraction): -5 x 2.0 mL grinding tubes (alternatively 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes) -5 mL sterile phospate buffered saline -1 x 4mm and 2 x 3mm steel grinding beads (alternatively 1 x sterile pestle for manual homogenization) -Sterile surface for handling frass (e.g. parafilm or petri dish) -1 x sterile forceps (or reusable forceps sterilised between each pooled sample) -1 x 10 mL graduated centrifuge tube (ideally screw-top) -1 x 2.0 mL round-bottomed microcentrifuge tube -DNeasy PowerSoil Pro kit (Qiagen Cat. 47014/6) -Molecular Grade water (MG H20) -WarmStart® Colorimetric LAMP 2X Master Mix with UDG (NEB Cat. M1804S/L) -LAMP Primers (IDT): Serr_ureD_F3: ATCGCCTGACGCTCGA Serr_ureD_B3: TAGAGCAGCGTCGCCGT Serr_ureD_FIP: CTGCATCTGCGCCGCGTA-GCCTGCGGGCATGTCA Serr_ureD_BIP: TCTGGAGATGATGCCCGATCCG-CGTAATGCGGGTATCGGTAA Serr_ureD_LF: TGGCGTGGATCTTGGTCG Serr_ureD_LB: CTGCGGTTCGCGCTTCA -3 x 0.2 mL PCR tubes

Conduct cell disruption and lysis by shaking the PowerBead tube in the Pac Lab Tissue Homogenizer or Qiagen Tissue Lyser II at 25 Hz for 10 mins. If no Tissue Homogenizer or Tissue Lyser is available a horizontal vortex at max speed for at least 10 min may be used.

Discard the spin column. The DNA is now contained in the flow-though and ready to be used. If not using immediately, store at -20ºC. Measure the concentration and quality of extracted DNA using spectrophotometry (e.g. Thermo Fisher Nanodrop or Implen Nanophotometer).

steps.title: Sample Collection and Storage
steps.instruction: Collect 300 mg of fresh frass sample per DNA extraction and store at 20ºC until processing.

steps.title: Prepare DNA Extraction Materials
steps.instruction: Gather and prepare the necessary reagents and consumables for the DNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Ensure Solution CD2 is stored at 4ºC; all other PowerSoil Pro kit reagents should be at room temperature.
If Solution CD3 has precipitated, heat it at 60ºC until dissolved.
Prepare the following hardware: 1 x 2.0 mL PowerBead tube, 2 x 2.0 mL microcentrifuge tubes, 1 x MB Spin Column, 2 x 2.0 mL collection tubes, and 1 x 1.5 mL elution tube.
Briefly spin the PowerBead Pro tube to settle the beads at the bottom.

steps.title: Sample Distribution and Homogenization
steps.instruction: Distribute the frass sample into grinding tubes and homogenize in PBS.

substeps.instruction: Add 1.0 mL sterile phosphate buffered saline (PBS) to five 2.0 mL grinding tubes (or 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes for manual homogenization).
Tip frass onto a sterile surface and use sterile forceps to add approximately 60 mg frass to each of the five tubes (300 mg total).
If using a tissue homogenizer, add 1 x 4mm and 2 x 3mm steel grinding beads to the tubes.
Homogenize samples using a Pac Lab Homogenizer on 'Plant Stem' (60 Hz for 60 sec x 3 with 15 sec pause) or 'Plant Leaf' (60 Hz for 45 sec x 3 with 15 sec pause) protocols.
If homogenizing manually, use a sterile pestle to crush the sample in each tube until well homogenized; a 100 µL pipette tip can be used to assist.

steps.title: Bacterial Concentration
steps.instruction: Separate bacterial cells from the frass matrix through centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the contents of all five grinding tubes into one 10 mL graduated centrifuge tube.
Shake the 10 mL tube well to mix.
Centrifuge the tube at 500 x g for 5 mins using a large swing bucket centrifuge. (Alternative: stand upright at 4ºC for 60 min to allow pellet to settle without mixing again).
Using a 1000 µL pipette tip, transfer up to 1.8 mL (2 x 900 µL) of supernatant to a clean 2.0 mL round-bottom microcentrifuge tube, aspirating close to the pellet.
Pellet the supernatant at up to 16000 x g at room temperature for 5 mins.
Carefully discard most of the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Repeat the transfer and pelleting process (Steps 9-11) once or twice more to maximize bacterial yield.

steps.title: Cell Lysis and DNA Purification
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from the concentrated bacterial pellet using the PowerSoil Pro kit.

substeps.instruction: Re-homogenize the bacterial pellet in 800 µL of Solution CD1 using a 1000 µL pipette tip, then transfer to a PowerBead tube and shake briefly.
Centrifuge the PowerBead tube at 15000 x g for 1 min and transfer the supernatant (approx. 500-700 µL) to a clean 2.0 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 200 µL Solution CD2, mix by gentle pipetting, centrifuge at 15000 x g for 1 min, and transfer up to 700 µL of supernatant to a clean 2.0 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 600 µL Solution CD3 and mix by gentle pipetting.
Load 660 µL of lysate into an MB Spin Column and centrifuge at 15000 x g for 1 min; discard flow-through and repeat to ensure all lysate has passed through.
Place the spin column into a 2.0 mL collection tube, add 500 µL Solution EA, centrifuge at 15000 x g for 1 min, and discard flow-through.
Place the spin column back into the same 2.0 mL collection tube, add 500 µL Solution C5, centrifuge at 15000 x g for 1 min, and discard flow-through.
Place the spin column into a clean 2.0 mL collection tube and centrifuge at 16000 x g for 2 min.
Transfer the spin column to a clean 1.5 mL elution tube, add 100 µL MG H2O to the center of the white filter membrane, and centrifuge at 15000 x g for 1 min.

steps.title: LAMP Reagent Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the primers, positive control, and master mix.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 25X LAMP Primer Mix using the LAMP worksheet (store at -20ºC).
Prepare a positive control of Serratia ureilytica AM923 DNA at approximately 50 ng/µL (store at 4°C for up to 7 days).
Prepare the working Master Mix using MG H2O, 1 X LAMP Master Mix, and 1 X LAMP Primer Mix according to the LAMP worksheet.

steps.title: LAMP Assay Setup and Incubation
steps.instruction: Set up the reaction tubes and incubate to amplify DNA.

substeps.instruction: Vortex the working Master Mix thoroughly and spin briefly.
Transfer 23 µL of Master Mix to each PCR tube.
Add 2 µL of MG H2O to negative control tubes and close caps.
Add 1 µL DNA sample to each tube, loading positive controls last to minimize false positives.
Close caps snugly and briefly spin down the PCR tubes.
Incubate the assays for 30 min at 65ºC (using a PCR block, heat block, or hot water bath).

steps.title: Result Interpretation and Storage
steps.instruction: Analyze the color change and store products if necessary.

substeps.instruction: Interpret results by color: Yellow = Positive, Pink = Negative, Orange = Inconclusive.
Store LAMP products at 4ºC for several months; avoid room temperature to prevent pH-driven color change.
Exercise caution when opening tubes for agarose gel electrophoresis to avoid workspace contamination.
